title: Marinating Fundamentals: Base, Salt, Surface Area, and Browning
summary: Lan Lam outlines the core structure of marinades, emphasizing a water-based base and salt as must-haves, with oil, sugar, and flavorings as optional add-ons. Using Dan Souza’s skillet chicken fajitas as an example, she walks through how base liquid and salt enable even flavor and juiciness, how to maximize surface contact by thinning or pounding meat, and how to time and cook marinated meat for a browned exterior and juicy interior. The video also covers safe reuse of marinade (boil to kill microbes) and practical guidelines for customizing marinades while keeping the core ratios intact. Practical steps include dry-patting before cooking, searing in a smoking-hot pan, finishing in a low-heat oven, resting the meat, and slicing across the grain to finish with flavorful pan juices.

sections.title: Marinade concept and must-have base
concepts: base liquid and salt as must-haves
sections.description: Introduces marinades as purposeful mixtures rather than random combos, with a water-based base and salt as essential components. Notes there isn’t a universal ratio and sets up the framework for building marinades.

sections.title: Must-haves and add-ons: base, salt, oil, sugar, flavorings
concepts: lime juice as base in Dan Souza’s fajitas
salt and ions for seasoning and moisture retention
oil for even cooking and browning
sections.description: Details the must-have base (water-based liquids) and salt, with lime juice as the example base. Describes optional additions: oil, sugar, and flavorings, and explains that most flavorings stay on the surface unless certain ingredients (garlic, glutamates) behave differently.

sections.title: Surface focus and marination timing concepts
sections.description: Explains that marinades primarily flavor the surface and emphasizes the fixed role of the base, salt, and proffered flavorings. Introduces practical timing considerations for marinating thin cuts to avoid texture degradation from acids.

sections.title: Prep for browning: thinning cuts and drying
concepts: drying before cooking to maximize Maillard browning
sections.description: Demonstrates thinning chicken breasts to about 1/2 inch to shorten salt travel distance and increase surface area for flavor uptake. Highlights skirt steak as an alternative with naturally larger surface area. Emphasizes patting dry before cooking to promote browning.

sections.title: Cooking method: high heat, browning, and gentle finish
sections.description: Outlines a two-stage cooking approach: sear on a smoking-hot skillet to develop a char, then transfer to a low-heat oven (200°F) to finish gently and preserve juiciness.

sections.title: Rest, slice, and glaze with pan juices
sections.description: Rest the cooked meat to retain moisture, then slice into thin strips and return to the skillet to coat with flavorful pan juices.

sections.title: Guidelines for customizing and retaining core ratios
concepts: retaining salt, liquid, and protein ratios
include sugar and oil for browning and even cooking
sections.description: Provides rules for customizing marinades while preserving core ratios. Advises keeping the proportion of water-based liquid, salt, and protein fixed and explains when to keep sugar and oil in to support browning and even cooking. Encourages flavor experimentation.

sections.title: Closing notes and engagement
sections.description: Wraps up with encouragement to comment on preferred marinades and to subscribe and visit Cook's Illustrated for more recipes.
